items.title: Roy Haynes — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He [Panama Francis] used to play with Lucky Millinder a lot. He told me that they would always wait in the front row...

ctx.x: In the morning. A.M. I don’t remember exactly. But I mean, if it was a hot show, where the people were coming, they’d have lines, so they would do – they would add shows. It wouldn’t be a contract saying you had to do this amount. They would add. Every time you come off, you’d see what time the half was – the half hour before the show. So I’m this youngster, playing with Luis Russell’s band. Nervous, yeah. Playing a show. I learned one thing with Luis Russell. He says, “If you ever get lost, lose the meter, or…

how I learned to play free, because you don’t give no definite beat. You just let it flow. So I got that from Luis Russell, when you roll. Anyhow, many years later, after I became – I’m in my thirties or forties. I’m with Panama Francis. Panama was one of the hot drummers from that area. He played with Cab [Calloway]. He used to play with Lucky Millinder a lot. He told me that they would always wait in the front row – a group of drummers – so if the drummer couldn’t play the show, they would get the gig for the…
